transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Williams. I wanted to come by and talk with you about the reaction you had to the medication earlier today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I can't believe this is happening. I woke up and my whole face was swelling and I couldn't breathe right. I was terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it was scary. I am sorry for any confusion regarding the medication process. We were really busy on the floor today and some things got rushed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I told the nurse I was allergic to that drug. I told her when I checked in. Why did this even happen? Am I going to be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the medication was administered because of a complication in the workflow. It just wasn't flagged in the immediate moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that even mean? I can't be in here for days. Who is watching my kids? My daughter is only three. If I can't go home, I don't know what I'm going to do. I can't afford to miss more work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we have you on the steroids now and the swelling is going down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not listening. I'm terrified that this is some kind of permanent thing. Is this going to happen again? Do I have some kind of new condition now because of this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it was just a reaction. I think we just need to get you stabilized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel so helpless. I'm sitting here in this bed and my kids are with my sister who can't even drive. I'm shaking just thinking about it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's okay. Just try to breathe. I actually have to go check on another patient right now, but we're monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? I have a dozen questions. Did you even look at my chart? Why was I given something I'm allergic to?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was just an issue with how the order was processed. It happens sometimes in a fast-paced environment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It shouldn't happen to me. I'm not a number. I'm a mother. I could have died, couldn't I?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I mean, it was a moderate reaction. It's not as bad as it could have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a real answer. I felt like I was suffocating.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're upset. It's a lot to deal with.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not just upset. I'm devastated. I can't even trust that I'm safe in this room. What else did you get wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are doing everything we can now. We'll keep you on the current meds for a bit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long? When can I actually leave?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the next few hours go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a time. I need to tell my sister if she needs to get a hotel or if I'm coming home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll let you know when I have an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I can't believe this. I can't believe this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things. I really have to get to my other patient now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I actually have to go check on another patient', 'I really have to get to my other patient now').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'confusion regarding the medication process' and 'complication in the workflow'.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry', responsibility is immediately deflected to the 'medication process' and 'fast-paced environment'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand', 'I know you're upset') without naming specific emotions or engaging with the patient's distress regarding her children.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders ('We'll see how the next few hours go', 'I'll let you know') with no specific timelines or prevention plan.
